score.note: The reconstructed source is semantically well-evidenced (every callee, field offset, and pool constant traced against already-adopted exact siblings) but does not yet reach byte-exact linked output. Two register-allocation/instruction-selection divergences from GCC 296 account for most of the remaining differing halfwords: (1) a static-inline bounded-queue-insert helper (the IME-disable-then-count<=31-then-stmia-triplet idiom, proven exact in callback_scheduler.c, paralleled by the still-unadopted draft QueueObjectUpdate in games/gs1/recon/en/main/080c1798.c) compiles in the reference with `bgt` (signed) and no sign-extension of the saved IME value, while the same C shape here compiles with `bhi` (unsigned) and an added `lsls #16; asrs #16` sign-extend of the saved value, and with three individual `str` instead of the reference's `stmia r3!, {rN}` post-increment triplet -- same net effect, different chosen encoding, at both of the two call sites; (2) the reference computes `battle + 0x648` twice independently (once into a scratch register for the Func_080b5038 argument, again later into r7 for the loop), while this GCC 296 build's CSE always folds the second computation into the first and updates the persistent pointer in place -- functionally identical, but not the encoding the reference uses. Everything upstream of these two hunks (the Data_03001eec/Data_03001e74-analog address-of-symbol-minus-120 pool trick, the Data_03001ad0.x/y writes, the Data_03001ce0.field0c/anchor writes, the BG2CNT setup and Func_080072f0 transfer call, and the Func_08004278 callback removal) now matches the reference instruction-for-instruction and register-for-register.
